scenario: A confectionery analyst examines craft chocolate brands currently in national retail, all of which survived early-phase attrition. Mean shelf-life score (a composite retail metric) is 5.5 (σ=1.2); the retail-entry threshold is 3.0. The true mean score across all brands that launched is of interest.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

question: (a) Assuming retail shelf-life score is normally distributed with σ=1.2 score points, solve for the pre-filter true mean μ such that E[X|X>3.0]=5.5. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much does the observed (survivor) mean overstate the pre-filter true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: The craft chocolate brands in retail after early exits retail shelf-life score set is a truncated-normal sample above the 3.0 threshold. Solving E[X|X>3.0]=μ+σφ((3.0−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((3.0−μ)/σ)=5.5 gives μ≈5.4379. Only 97.9% of all original units survived; the survivor mean overstates the true mean by 0.0621 score points.

naive_answer: The true mean retail shelf-life score is 5.5 score points because that is the observed average among craft chocolate brands in retail after early exits.
naive_trap: Survival/publication filters truncate the distribution from below; the observed mean among survivors is a conditional expectation and systematically overstates the pre-filter population mean.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter is equivalent to truncated-normal sampling above threshold=3.0. (2) Truncated mean equation: μ+σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=5.5. (3) Numerically solve with brentq → μ≈5.4379. (4) Fraction surviving: Φ̄((3.0−5.4379)/σ)≈0.9789.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 5.5,1.2,3.0
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-5.4379)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.9789)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
